about: What the deploy kit needs that no Worker's config can say (deploy/facts.ts reads it, with the six wrangler.jsonc). Everything a config says (each Worker's name, bindings, required secrets, bucket and queues, Durable Object migrations, and the order its bindings set) is read from the config; the shared apps' signing secrets from the file its workers entry names; the doors' public identity from contract/identity.json. Each entry here carries its reason.

namespaces.why: A config names a KV namespace by an id the account gives when it is made (a placeholder as checked in), never by its title: the kit finds each by its title, or makes it, and fills the id in. One title per binding name: every Worker's CONTROL is the one namespace.

workers.why: What the kit gives a Worker that its config cannot say, by its folder. identity: it serves contract/identity.json, so it deploys with the owner issuer and WorkOS's record (its vars OWNER_ISSUER and UPSTREAM), mode routes hands it identity.json's routes and egress custom domain, and the probe the sign-in's two. shared_apps: its file of the shared apps, whose signing secrets it holds when each is given (no config requires them: without one, that app's door refuses loudly). Exactly one Worker serves the identity; a Worker not named here takes neither.

secret_order.why: The order the kit lists and sets the Workers' secrets in, so the plan names them in it. A config says which secrets its Worker needs, not this order. The codemode Worker holds no secret, so it is not here: its existence is read when it deploys.

retired.why: The Workers the platform no longer has: the one way a platform Worker is deleted, so the cutover manifest names its Workers here. Each is deleted by the deploy step after every Worker is deployed, when the account's Workers listing holds it: by then no Worker of this tree binds it, and Cloudflare refuses the delete while any other Worker still references it (the kit never forces it) and deletes the Worker's own Durable Object namespaces with it. tinyassets-hooks is the code mode Worker's name before untangle B25: its VMs keep no state, so its objects go with it. An entry is deleted once a deploy has run it.

buckets.why: The R2 buckets the kit makes that no Worker binds, by what each holds (the name its reader takes it by, facts.ts --import), each made by dark's storage step when the account's listing lacks it, as the bound ones are. final_backup holds the off-site copy of the import window's final backup (import-window.yml, mode offsite): kept through the 14-day hold, then deleted with the old stack's final backup, on the founder's word (tasks.md section 9).

bucket_locks.why: The R2 buckets whose every object is kept, unchangeable and undeletable, for so many days, by the binding that binds each: a config names a bucket, not a lock on it. OPERATOR_LOG is the operator channel's audit log (doors/src/operator.ts): each message's acceptance record and answer, kept a year (d3 §G). dark's storage step makes each the bucket's one lock rule, over every object, when the bucket holds no rule or another.

made.why: The secrets the founder's setup makes (scripts/platform_setup.py), each by its kind: mac is 32 random bytes in base64url, token a random URL-safe token, keyring a first keyring in keyring-new's shape (rotated only by adding a key). A config names a secret, not how its value is made; every other secret comes from its vendor or a shared app.
